chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakil narrated to me, and he said:

Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'dabadi narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from al-Bazanti ibn Ali, from Hariz, from some of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: 'The oath that consigns [one] to Hell is when a man swears falsely regarding the right of a Muslim, specifically concerning the withholding of his wealth.'

key_terms.الْیَمِینُ الْغَمُوسُ: The oath that consigns to Hell
key_terms.تُوجِبُ النَّارَ: Consigns to Hell / Makes Hell obligatory

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of Yamin al-Ghamus in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-Amal*, this narration defines *Yamin al-Ghamus* as a specific false oath that guarantees entry into Hell, emphasizing the gravity of depriving a Muslim of their rightful property. This concept is central to Shia jurisprudence regarding *Yamin* (oaths) and highlights the spiritual peril of using Allah’s name to unjustly withhold wealth, linking verbal transgression directly to material injustice.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 9. It was narrated to me by Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakil who said

it was narrated to me by Ali b. al-Hussain al-Sa’dabadi from Ahmad b. Abi Abdillah from al-Bazanti b. Ali from Hareez from some of his companions from Abi Abdillah (a.s.) who said: “If a man swears falsely due to which there is a loss of wealth or right of a Muslim, he has made Hell obligatory on himself.”
